clue.text: This tease contrived to produce delays

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so the letters of the two words are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A flirt's teasing is deliberately staged to hold things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived to produce' rearranges THIS and TEASE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause before acting, so someone who hesitates delays; same verb form.

clue.text: Some animals reported and caught

indicators.note: a report passes on news by word of mouth, so the animal word counts by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a herd is a group of animals such as cattle

explanation.surface: A news item about a group of animals that were captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns HERD into a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb of listening: if you caught what someone said, you made it out by ear.

clue.text: Home for animals on the agenda for cutter

parts.note: a sty is the pen where pigs are kept
items on the agenda are on the list

explanation.surface: A meeting agenda includes a farm building and a cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Recurring 'home for animals' phrase gives a different animal home in each clue; here the pig's.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairdresser who cuts hair is often called a stylist; 'cutter' describes the job.

clue.text: Instant home for animals created from array of children's products

parts.note: an instant is a moment or point in time
a stable houses horses

explanation.surface: A building for horses made out of a display of toys and goods for kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'products' are the results of multiplication, which children learn as a grid of numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The multiplication chart children memorise sets out the results of multiplying numbers, a grid of mathematical products.

clue.text: Catch fish rising over home for animals less than a dozen times

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits over, so before, the other
in a down clue a word going up is read from bottom to top, so the catching word is turned round

parts.note: to net fish is to catch them
a fold is a pen for sheep

explanation.surface: Fish leaping above a sheep pen are caught nearly a dozen times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NET upwards to make TEN; 'over' puts it above FOLD in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten times as much is a multiple a little under twelve, so the word for tenfold fits 'less than a dozen times'.

clue.text: One takes fall on head after this last animal

indicators.note: the headland word comes after the single letter
the final letter of the word this is taken

parts.note: a cape is a headland jutting into the sea
a goat is a farm animal

explanation.surface: Someone falls headfirst after this last animal does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes the S of 'this'; 'after' puts the headland behind it. 'fall' suggests a tumble, but it is the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes the fall bears the blame for others, the classic role of a whipping boy.

clue.text: Metal in cable carries live power

parts.note: copper, chemical symbol Cu, is the metal used in electrical cable
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A copper electrical cable carrying a live current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' joins the two pieces. In maths the cube of a number is that number raised to the third power.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube is a third power in mathematics, so 'power' covers it as an example.

clue.text: Spooner's traditional cover for tradesman's entry into home for animals

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: a flat cap is the cloth cap traditionally worn by working men
a flat cap is the cloth cap traditionally worn by working men

explanation.surface: Through the tradesman's entrance comes a workman in his customary headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the openings of FLAT and CAP gives CAT and FLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hinged door lets a pet cat into and out of the house; the house is the pet's home.

clue.text: Home for animals of the ocean under cover (suitable for fish)

indicators.note: in a down entry the lower piece comes after, so the sea word follows

parts.note: batter is the coating for fried fish
the ocean is the sea

explanation.surface: An animal shelter at the bottom of the sea, protected by a coating meant for fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battersea Dogs and Cats Home is a famous animal rescue centre in London; 'under' sets the ocean piece below the batter in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The London rescue centre for stray dogs and cats takes its name from the district where it stands.

clue.text: Slay damn evil wolf

indicators.note: something evil is twisted or corrupt, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A cry to kill a wicked wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evil' rearranges SLAY and DAMN together. 'wolf' is not the animal but a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf is a man who pursues women, a womaniser, the same as one who is popular with them.

clue.text: Sharp taste spread round middle of mouth

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the central letter
letters spread about are scattered and so rearranged
the central letter of the word mouth is taken

explanation.surface: A sharp flavour fills the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' turns TASTE into ASTTE; 'round' wraps it around U, from 'middle of mouth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and sharp are synonyms for being clever and perceptive.

clue.text: Off-the-cuff remarks in Asian capital should end party excess at last

indicators.note: the capital, or first, letter of Asian is taken
the final letter of should is taken

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal, a political party

indicators.note: the final letter of excess is taken

explanation.surface: Improvised quips in an Asian city say the party's excesses should stop at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian capital' looks like a city but gives only A; then D, LIB and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvised remarks made without preparation are ad-libs, Latin for 'at pleasure'.

clue.text: Rests on Boatman to get stuck into problem with resolve

indicators.note: the setter's letter is placed inside the shuffled word
a problem with something makes it go wrong, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter tackles a problem with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem with' rearranges RESOLVE into OVERLES; 'to get stuck into' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlie something is to lie on top of it, so overlies means rests on.

clue.text: Held in home for animals: a ram

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for livestock
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A ram is kept in an animal enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a ram' gives TUP, a dialect word for a male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings that are pent-up are held in or suppressed.

clue.text: Proclaiming something in City bank

indicators.note: the thing word is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a noun is a word for something, a thing
ING is a Dutch bank

explanation.surface: Something hidden in a London bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the thing word inside the City abbreviation, split after its E. ING is a Dutch banking group.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to state or pronounce formally, so proclaiming works as a synonym.

clue.text: Casual racism: it follows coppers split by colour

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the coin abbreviation

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated p

indicators.note: something casual is loose and offhand, so the letters are loosely rearranged

explanation.surface: Offhand racism comes after the police are torn apart by colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casual' rearranges the letters of 'racism: it', which 'follows' the penny. 'coppers' suggests police, but means pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism separates white light into its colours, so prismatic means split into a spectrum.

clue.text: Act before or after getting support for entry into home

indicators.note: the act word is placed before the next piece

parts.note: to do is to act
post is Latin for after, as in postwar

explanation.surface: A discussion about acting before or after getting help to enter a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' puts the act word ahead of 'or'. 'support for entry into home' is the definition, not a hint at 'post' as a support.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorpost is the upright that supports a door frame, the entry into a house.

clue.text: Home for party animals (nearly 50 inside)

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the number goes inside the animals word

parts.note: mice are small animals
IL is 49 in Roman numerals, just under fifty

explanation.surface: A home for party animals where nearly fifty people are inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly 50' is a joke: the Roman form of 49 by the subtraction rule sits 'inside' the small animals. 'party animals' is a misleading phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is a home, a person's legal place of residence.

clue.text: Fool's gold perhaps gets one right on the heart, losing head

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped from the heart word

parts.note: the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Fool's gold may hit someone right in the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes C from CORE, leaving ORE. Fool's gold is pyrite, an iron mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrite, nicknamed fool's gold, is iron sulphide and an example of a mineral iron is mined from.

clue.text: To counter racism, he wrote novel Noise about liberal left

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the two abbreviations
novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: An anti-racist author's novel about a liberal on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges NOISE into EISON; 'about' wraps it around LL. Ralph Ellison wrote Invisible Man, about racism in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Ellison was the African American author of Invisible Man, a novel attacking racial prejudice.

clue.text: Disturbance in the area? Navy surrounds Asian capital

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters of the word are reordered
the navy abbreviation goes around the area letter

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Unrest in a region as warships encircle an Asian capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbance in' shuffles 'the' into TEH; 'surrounds' puts the navy around the area letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the capital of Iran, a country in Asia.

clue.text: Why did the naughty cow enter the house?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go into the house word

parts.note: home is a house

indicators.note: naughty means badly behaved, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why a cow got into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges COW into WCO, which 'enter's HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase is a casual way of asking for a reason, the same as asking why.

clue.text: Casual home for some animals

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: only some of the letters of animals are kept, the inner run after the opening three, dropping the final S too

explanation.surface: A relaxed home for certain animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home for some animals' looks like the theme phrase for an animal shelter, but it is wordplay word by word; 'some' keeps only MAL from 'animals'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal and casual both describe something relaxed, not following strict rules.

clue.text: Watch worn on top of knitted cuff

indicators.note: worn suggests something battered out of shape, so the letters are reordered
the first letter of knitted is taken

explanation.surface: A wristwatch worn above a knitted sleeve cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' rearranges WATCH into THWAC; 'top of' gives K from 'knitted'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuff is to strike with an open hand, as is to give a hard blow.

clue.text: See 3
Boatman's cut of film Tin Man, criminally bad

parts.note: a can is the tin in which film is stored
Al Capone was a notorious gangster

explanation.surface: The setter's edit of a film about the Tin Man, which was dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: A cut is a man-made waterway, used by boatmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial waterway, an excavated channel called a cut.

clue.text: Animal escaped into gorge?

parts.note: a pig is an animal
an escaped animal is out

explanation.surface: An animal broke free and ran into a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a ravine but is the verb, to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig out is an informal idiom for eating to excess, the same as to gorge.

clue.text: Alternative Gothic writer returns an invitation one can't refuse

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or alternative
Edgar Allan Poe wrote Gothic tales

indicators.note: the short word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: An alternative Gothic author comes back with an offer you cannot decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns AN to NA. A subpoena is a court order to appear, so the 'invitation' cannot be refused.
explanation.definitionFit: A subpoena is a legal summons to attend court, which must be obeyed, a joking sort of invitation.

clue.text: One at home in a bog (really evil type)

definitions.text: One at home in a bog (really evil type)

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, across the word break

explanation.surface: A creature living in a swamp is a truly wicked sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: Shrek, the cartoon monster, lives in a swamp, and folk-tale monsters of his kind are cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: A brutish man-eating giant of fairy tales, like Shrek in his swamp, is a truly wicked creature.

clue.text: Fish listen to one dance tune, then another

indicators.note: listening means the words are heard, not read, so the dance names count by sound

parts.note: the conga and the reel are two dances

explanation.surface: Fish listen to dance music, one tune after another.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech CONGA REEL sounds just like the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger is a large sea eel, a kind of fish.
